newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes sharply firmer on GDP euphoria.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes sharply firmer on GDP euphoria.

text.p: The Mexican peso regained ground lost earlier in the week and closed very firm on Wednesday on market euphoria over strong GDP figures, traders said.

"The market was very busy and the peso gained much ground," a trader said."The GDP figures triggered a new inflow of capital, in addition to the dollar influx coming into the market from corporations changing to pesos to meet tax bills."
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 3.45 and 3.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.7640/7.665 and 7.7615 per dollar.
Mexico's Finance Ministry announced shortly before the foreign exchange markets opened that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased 5.1 percent in 1996, compared to 1995.
Traders said the GDP news outweighed the potentially adverse effect of a fall in primary interest rates at Tuesday night's government securities auction.

Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 19.46 percent, a fall of 23 basis points from last week and their lowest level since a fumbled devaluation of the peso sent Mexican financial markets tumbling in December 1994.
Dealers also noted that foreign investment may have flown into Mexico in the wake of an announcement of benign U.S. consumer inflation figures.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.7820/7.7850 per dollar.
